'''Derrick White''' (born July 2, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played three years of college basketball for the [[University of Colorado Colorado Springs]] (UCCS) before transferring to the [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] [[University of Colorado Boulder]] for his final season. 

==College career==
White, a [[combo guard]], was lightly recruited out of [[Legend High School]] in [[Parker, Colorado]], receiving no scholarship offers from any four-year institutions. At the time of his high school graduation, which fell about two months before his 18th birthday, he was barely 6 feet tall—after growing two inches during his senior year.<ref name="Bright spot">{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=Derrick White A Bright Spot In Probable Lost Season For Buffs|url=http://denver.cbslocal.com/2017/03/07/derrick-white-university-colorado-buffaloes/|accessdate=May 6, 2017|work=denver.cbs.local.com|date=March 7, 2017}}</ref> The only head coach at a four-year school who showed sustained interest in White was Jeff Culver, then the head coach at the Denver campus of [[Johnson & Wales University]], a non-scholarship [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] member better known for its culinary program. By the time White was preparing to make his college decision, Culver was hired as head coach at [[NCAA Division II]] [[Colorado–Colorado Springs Mountain Lions men's basketball|Colorado–Colorado Springs]], and offered White a room and board stipend for his freshman season.<ref name=Eisenberg>{{cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/sports/news/colorados-derrick-white-went-unrecruited-unlikely-nba-prospect-170715016.html |title=How Colorado's Derrick White went from unrecruited to unlikely NBA prospect |first=Jeff |last=Eisenberg |publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |date=May 8, 2017 |accessdate=May 9, 2017}}</ref> Culver was only expecting White to become a starter late in his college career. He was aware that White's father had a late growth spurt in college, and also knew that doctors had projected White to potentially reach 6'5".<ref name=Eisenberg/> As it turned out, White reached that potential height by the time he enrolled at Colorado–Colorado Springs.<ref name="Bright spot"/> With his newfound size and athleticism, White became a star at UCCS, starting every game of his three-year career and left as the school's career leader in points (1,912) and assists (343). In his junior season, he averaged 25.8 points, 7.3 rebounds and 5.2 assists for the Mountain Lions, leading the team to the [[2015 NCAA Division II Men's Basketball Tournament|2015 NCAA Tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Jhabvala|first1=Nicki|title=Derrick White, a 3-year standout guard at UCCS, transfers to Colorado |url=http://www.denverpost.com/2015/04/19/derrick-white-a-3-year-standout-guard-at-uccs-transfers-to-colorado/|accessdate=May 6, 2017|work=[[Denver Post]]|date=April 19, 2015}}</ref> He was named an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].

Following this season, White opted to transfer to Division I [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] to test his skills in the [[Pac-12 Conference]], one of the top college leagues in the country.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Barnhouse|first1=Wendell|title=How former DII All-American Derrick White became Colorado’s ‘best player’|url=https://www.fanragsports.com/cbb/former-dii-american-derrick-white-became-colorados-best-player/|accessdate=May 6, 2017|work=fanragsports.com|date=December 21, 2016}}</ref> After sitting out the 2015–16 season per [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] rules, White excelled in his lone season with the Buffaloes, averaging 18.1 points, 4.1 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game. He was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and a member of the five-man All-Defensive team.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rooney|first1=Pat|title=Derrick White's lone season with CU Buffs reaps All-Pac-12, All-Defensive team honors|url=http://www.dailycamera.com/sports/ci_30839168/cu-buffs-derrick-white-named-all-pac-12?source=rss|accessdate=May 6, 2017|work=[[Daily Camera]]|date=March 6, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==
White was one of 60 NBA prospects invited to the 2017 [[NBA Draft Combine]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rooney|first1=Pat|title=Derrick White to represent CU at NBA draft combine|url=http://www.buffzone.com/mensbasketball/ci_30955305/derrick-white-represent-cu-buffs-at-nba-draft|accessdate=May 6, 2017|work=buffzone.com|date=April 29, 2017}}</ref> He was one of only 15 combine invitees who had not been [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] top-150 prospects in high school, and one of only three who did not sign with Division I programs out of high school. In addition, according to [[Yahoo! Sports]] writer Jeff Eisenberg, he was also "the only one who will use part of his first NBA contract to pay off student loans he accumulated paying for tuition at UCCS as a freshman."<ref name=Eisenberg/>
